messages:
Anna (DevEx): Quick design idea — what if the schema editor displayed a small "sample output" card inline next to each function definition? You could map output keys to UI labels there without opening the inspector.

Mike (Design): I like that. Inline card keeps context. Maybe show truncated JSON + a 'Map fields' CTA. Also keyboard nav: tab should move into the mapping grid.

Rachel (PM): Run history should record which function version produced the mapped output. Right now you can't tell which schema was used in a past run.

Gabe (Eng): Implementation note: we stream partial tokens, so the "sample output" should be the final normalized object saved at completion. We can attach it to run metadata: "final_structured_output": {...}

Gabe (Eng): Also consider size — we should cap stored sample output (e.g., 2KB) and include a link to full artifact.

Mike (Design): Copy nit: CTA should read "Map output fields" not "Edit schema" — clearer for product folks. And microcopy under the card: "Matches keys from model response. Edit to shape downstream UI."

Anna (DevEx): Accessibility nits — when mapping grid opens, focus should move into the first input, and there should be aria-live region for validation messages. Color contrast for required badges is low on dark theme.

Rachel (PM): For run history UX, propose a compact timeline view with inline diffs for mapped fields: show old->new mapping per run and which function version changed it. :eyes:

Mike (Design): Sketches attached (will drop in Figma). For collapsed state, show single-line summary: "Mapped 5 fields • function@v2 • 120ms". Expand reveals mapping table + sample output.

CI Bot: build/test/playground-schema  — ✅ all checks passed (build #4312).

Anna (DevEx): Next steps: Mike to update mock with keyboard flows, Gabe to validate metadata size and storage, Rachel to write acceptance criteria for run history diffs. I'll capture copy updates and accessibility checklist.

Rachel (PM): Timeline: can we prototype in next sprint? We need this for a demo with customer alpha.

Gabe (Eng): I'll spike storage approach this week and report back by Thu.

Mike (Design): I'll push updated Figma by EOD tomorrow.

Anna (DevEx): Awesome, thanks everyone. :rocket:
